title: Prescriber Statement Wait Counted on Member-Opened Exception Requests (Formulary Benefit)
content:
A member who opens their own exception request under the Formulary Benefit still needs the prescriber's supporting statement. A statement wait is therefore added to the member's wait, the number of days compared with the member's days left. How much is added depends on two things: whether a statement for the drug has recently been received, and whether the prescriber already has a coverage review case for the drug open with the Utilization Management Program.

**Records read.**
- Statements received for the drug on any of the member's exception requests.
- The latest coverage review case for the drug opened for the member under the Utilization Management Program, with the prescriber who opened it and when.
- The prescriber on the member's latest Home Delivery Pharmacy prescription for the drug.

**Lookbacks.** The statement lookback is **12** months and the prescriber-case lookback is **12** months. An item is within a lookback when it lies fewer whole months than 12 before the handling date.

## Clause

| Statement for the drug received within 12 months | Latest review case for the drug opened by the prescriber on the latest home delivery prescription, within 12 months | Statement wait added |
|---|---|---|
| no | no | the formulary's full wait for a prescriber statement, in days |
| no | yes (the clinical file is already with Northbridge Rx) | **5** days, the engaged-prescriber wait |
| yes | any | none |

**The formulary's full wait for a prescriber statement (calendar days):**

| Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

*Hypothetical.* Take a member on the Northbridge Standard Formulary with no statement for the drug in the past year. If the latest review case for the drug was opened two months ago by a different prescriber, 14 days are added. If it was opened by the prescriber on the latest home delivery prescription, 5 days are added. If it was opened by that prescriber 12 whole months ago, it is outside the lookback, and 14 days are added.
